scope: October 13, 2025 Law: common rules, four base factions, Fall/Winter, Thief/Tinker/Ranger, dominance and coalition; excludes expansion systems, second Vagabond, hirelings, landmarks, bots and Advanced Setup.
method: Read complete applicable extracted source and directly rechecked corresponding PDF pages 1-10, 24-28. Read only the four permitted QA inputs. Checked all 80 actual question requests against the source and key; ledger claims and contextual expected-answer details did not independently establish coverage. No reader responses, grades, summary, earlier review/audit files or historical benchmark files read.

findings.finding: Q04 broadly requests how crafting costs work, but its expected answer only says Vagabond uses hammers and can reactivate pawn. It omits the explicit one-hammer-per-crafting-icon payment in 9.5.8. Reusing the pawn could be read as also reusing one hammer to pay all icons, unless this independent resource cost is required by the key.
findings.actual_request_analysis: An unqualified crafting-cost request includes Vagabond payment. This uses the same scope reading as the documented Q37 production correction. Q56 asks mixed-suit legality, repeated pawn use and immediate crafted-item use; its true per-icon cost sentence is contextual rather than an independently requested cost test. Therefore tighten Q04 grading in a new version rather than add another cost question.
findings.source_quote: Craft a card by exhausting one H per crafting icon it has.
findings.recommended_action: Version the Q04 expected answer to require one ready undamaged hammer per crafting icon; preserve all existing benchmark versions and historical scores.

old_entry.expected_answer: Activate crafting pieces matching icons; each piece once per turn. Card suit is not its crafting cost. Immediate effect resolves then card discarded; item must be in supply or cannot craft. Persistent effect stays in play area; cannot craft identical effect already there. Vagabond uses hammers and can reactivate pawn.

new_entry.expected_answer: Activate crafting pieces matching every crafting icon; each piece may normally activate only once per turn. A crafting piece's suit is its clearing's suit, and the card's own suit is not its crafting cost. An item must be available in the map supply or that card cannot be crafted. Resolve an immediate effect and discard the card; a persistent effect stays in the play area, and an identical persistent effect already there prevents crafting another. For Vagabond crafting, exhaust one face-up, undamaged hammer per crafting icon; the pawn may be activated repeatedly, but its clearing must match every crafting icon. Reusing the pawn does not waive the hammer payment for each icon.

proposed_key_corrections.minimal_required_change: Replace Vagabond uses hammers and can reactivate pawn with Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per crafting icon to activate its pawn, which can be activated repeatedly; each icon still requires its own hammer payment.
proposed_key_corrections.novelty: No question novelty claimed: Q04 already asks crafting costs broadly. This is a source-backed omission in its grading target, not a new procedure request.

documented_correction_verification.reason: Its question asks when and how much wood the Marquise produces without a Birdsong restriction. The new entry correctly adds Daylight Overwork: spend matching sawmill-clearing card for one wood there. Eight-token finite supply, maximum placement and ordinary Evening draw/discard match source. Old/new entry verified against permitted correction record and source, without opening historical versions.

new_question_novelty_verification.reason: Q19 requests Strike target priority, not payment. Its contextual crossbow sentence does not establish an asked cost test. Q80 expressly requests the first Strike item/quantity payment, while Q75 concerns a different action and item. Readiness is context already tested by Q50; the novel requested rule is one crossbow for Strike.

zero_addition_pass_challenge.result: Zero new-question additions survives this independent challenge, but the final grading key is not complete: version Q04 before claiming full requested-and-graded coverage.
